objective: Sequential focused-task campaign to improve validated learning efficiency and higher-order quantitative-research capability.
process_conclusion: The audit confirms the frontier-first selection practice has a concrete qualitative advantage: recent activations closed five distinct new signal classes with decisive, independently verified verdicts and no equivalent re-tests, replacing the earlier pattern of repeatedly refining one MA(20/60) result from a queue. The controller's deterministic qualitative selector correctly ranked the OPEN LEARNING_PROCESS candidates on its first use, but its comparative effect is not yet measurable.
research_conclusion: COST_ROBUST within the existing cost model (independently verified): lookback 3/5/10 momentum segment medians are essentially unchanged at realistic and 2x stress costs; 9/10 assets have strictly positive lookback-5 segment medians at all three cost levels (verdict-independent), 6/10 retain a verdict-based positive REGIME_STABLE edge, lookback-ROBUST is 6/10, and the predeclared aggregate class is COST_ROBUST. Verdict flips (MSFT/JPM) are matched-null dispersion artifacts, not candidate degradation. Qualification: the engine applies slippage symmetrically (beneficial on sells), so the cost model is optimistic and adverse-slippage cost robustness remains UNVERIFIED; the momentum candidate stays admitted as candidate positive evidence with this qualification.
unverified: Adverse-slippage cost robustness: research/backtest/engine.py adds slippage to the fill price for both buys and sells (symmetric, favorable on sells), so slippage largely cancels over round trips and the realistic/stress results are optimistic (commission-dominated). A direction-dependent adverse-slippage cost model was not tested.

Causal attribution is observational: the frontier-first era has roughly seven activations versus roughly two opportunistic-era MA-refinement activations, with no control group and a toolkit-maturity confound, so the selector cannot be isolated as the sole cause of improved information flow.

Only the repository's 10 large-cap assets and one cost model were tested; no claim is made about other universes, other cost regimes, or live execution. The 2x stress level is a bounded stress, not an extreme-cost bound.

The 'no equivalent re-tests' judgment applies LEARNING_STATE learning rule 2 (new hypothesis, diagnostic purpose, data, verification need, or information objective); the momentum family has several variants that were accepted as distinct diagnostic purposes, but a stricter equivalence standard could reclassify some as near-duplicates.
The controller's formal task_rank selector has only one selection in this campaign, so its comparative advantage over opportunistic choice is UNVERIFIED pending at least three selections.

The synthetic perturbation sweep was not used for this task because the regime-switching generator contains no return autocorrelation (it validates tooling, not momentum cost robustness); the real-data matched-null sweep is the operative test.

The verdict-based per-asset classification is null-dispersion-sensitive: MSFT flips REGIME_STABLE -> REGIME_DEPENDENT and JPM flips REGIME_DEPENDENT -> REGIME_STABLE across cost levels with unchanged candidate medians. The verdict-independent strictly-positive-medians view (9/10 assets at all levels) is the more reliable reading and is recorded in the artifact.
